headline: Record underwriting and investment income lift core earnings
summary_short: Chubb's Q2 FY2026 net income was $2.85 billion ($7.30 diluted EPS), down 3.8% y/y on a smaller realized-gains benefit, while core operating income rose 14.6% y/y to $2.84 billion ($7.26/share) as P&C underwriting income jumped 18.8% to an 83.8% combined ratio and net investment income hit a record $1.76 billion.
summary_long: Core operating income rose 14.6% y/y to $2.84B ($7.26/share, +18.2%), driven by P&C underwriting income of $1.94B (+18.8%, 83.8% combined ratio) on lower catastrophe losses ($475M vs $630M) and stronger favorable reserve development ($283M vs $249M). Net investment income hit a record $1.76B, up 12.3%. Net premiums written rose 3.6% to $14.7B, led by Overseas General (+10.2%) and Life Insurance (+7.5%), while North America Commercial fell 2.3% on a deliberate large-account property pullback. GAAP net income fell 3.8% y/y to $2.85B on a smaller realized-gains benefit versus last year. Book value per share rose 12.3% y/y to $195.45. Chubb returned $1.37B to shareholders (buybacks $979M, dividends $395M). No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: GAAP net income declined y/y mainly because the prior-year quarter included a much larger after-tax realized-gains benefit ($539M vs $47M this quarter, per Chubb's own reconciliation table).
EPS fell less than net income (-0.7% vs -3.8%) because weighted-average diluted shares outstanding dropped to 391.3M from 403.8M on buybacks.
Growth was driven by consolidated net premiums written +3.6% to $14.7B (Overseas General +10.2%, Life +7.5%) and record net investment income of $1.76B, up 12.3%.
